sections.title: What to write in a LinkedIn connection request message
blocks: A useful connection note answers two questions quickly: how does this person know you, and why does connecting make sense now? A reference to the email they just sent is stronger than a generic compliment because the recipient can verify it immediately.

LinkedIn's current help page says a personalised invitation can contain up to 200 characters and recommends explaining how you found the person or what you share, why you want to connect and using a clear, polite tone. Every option the generator produces fits within that 200-character limit. The same page notes that free members can send only a limited number of invitations with a note each month (three when checked), while Premium members are not limited, so each note you do send should carry a recognisable reason. Check LinkedIn's current invitation guidance before relying on a limit, because product rules can change.

sections.title: Connection note examples by situation
list: After an email: mention the actual topic, not merely that they emailed you.
After a meeting: name the conversation or decision you want to remember.
After an event: use the session, roundtable or introduction rather than the event name alone.
After reading a post: identify the idea that changed or sharpened your view; avoid empty praise.
For collaboration: connect first and keep a detailed proposal for the follow-up conversation.

sections.title: What the generator deliberately avoids
blocks: It does not scrape a profile, read a private message, invent shared interests or send anything automatically. It also avoids a full sales pitch inside the invitation. A connection request is a small piece of context, not a substitute for a proposal or a consent signal for future outreach.

The result is deterministic: the same inputs produce the same family of notes. That keeps the tool private and makes every phrase inspectable, but you still need to edit the output for your voice and relationship.

faq.q: What is the LinkedIn connection note character limit?
faq.a: LinkedIn's help page listed 200 characters when this tool was checked on 29 October 2026. The generator keeps every option at or below that limit, but the counter in your own invitation dialog is authoritative.

faq.q: Does this tool use AI or upload my context?
faq.a: No. It combines inspected local templates in your browser. The recipient name, context and detail are not sent to SenderFinder or an AI provider.

faq.q: Will SenderFinder send a LinkedIn invitation automatically?
faq.a: No. The extension can open the profile and fill an editable note after you choose Connect, but it never clicks Connect or Send. You remain responsible for reviewing and sending the invitation.

faq.q: Should a connection request include a sales pitch?
faq.a: Usually not. Use the invitation to establish recognisable context. Save a detailed offer, request or proposal for a later conversation after the person chooses to connect.
